summary: Pavel Poucha was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Charles University (1924–1929) under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Hujer, later serving as Docent at the Oriental Institute (1948–1958).

Linguist Pavel Trost earned his PhD at Charles University under Friedrich Karl Slotty. He worked at the Moravian Library (1938–1944), lectured at Masaryk University (1945–1952), and served as Docent at Palacký University (1951–1956) and Charles University (1956–1975).
Pavle Jevtić worked in Indology and philosophy. He was a disciple of Dimitrije Mitrinović and completed his Ph.D. at SOAS University of London around 1923–1927.

Pavlo Grigorovič Ritter specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij at the University of Kharkiv, also studying under Karl Friedrich Geldner, and became a professor at the University of Kharkiv in 1921.

Working in linguistics and Indology, Pawan Goyal earned an M.Tech. from IIT Madras and a Ph.D. from the Max Planck Institute, where he was a postdoctoral associate in 2018. He has been affiliated with IIT Kharagpur (attested 2018–2025).

Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology, earning degrees from Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. At the University of Rangoon, he was Professor of Pali (1912) and Principal (1937–1946), later heading the Burma Historical Commission (1960–1964).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pedro Roca y López worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Juan Gelabert y Gordiola, earned a Dr.phil. at Complutense University of Madrid, and held posts as librarian at the University of Barcelona and the National Library of Spain.

id: P:Pedro Urbano González de la Calle
summary: Indologist and linguist Pedro Urbano González de la Calle earned his Ph.D. at Complutense University of Madrid under Mario Daza de Campos. He held professorships at Valencia, Madrid, Barcelona, Bogotá, UNAM, and El Colegio de México (1950–1965).

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a B.A. from National Taiwan University, she completed a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who previously served as professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington. He was also director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. A disciple of Chögyam Trungpa, she served as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center (1979–1984) and has been director and abbess of Gampo Abbey.
Pema Donyo Nyinje is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and his own students include Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Pema Gyaltsen worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and taught Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Pema Sherpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, attested in 2026 as a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pema Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn (attested 1982).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
